notes: Summary: OrbitPilot is building a low-latency IDE copilot (VSCode + internal web IDE). Primary constraint is UX: time-to-first-token (TTFT) must feel local. Target TTFT: <=50ms in ideal path, 50-120ms acceptable with graceful spinner. Jitter budget: <10–15ms for token arrival variance; tail-latency under 200ms for 95th perc. They want streaming partial completions (token deltas) and positional merges for live edit flow. Token-budgeting: per-session soft budget 2k–5k tokens, with hard backpressure and graceful degrade to smaller model or cached prefix when exceeded. Model/versioning: want strict model pinning (we can't have silent model upgrades), fast rollback, and canary rollouts for new weights. Prefer quantized 1.3B variant for local-feel but need fallback to 7B optimized variant during bursts. Deployment: leaning Dedicated for predictable latency, but legal pushing Private VPC / on-prem for code residency. Security: expect SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS, retention controls. SE notes: "If TTFT isn't stable UX will break — devs abandon completions" (quote from lead eng). POC asks: 1) run 2-week POC measuring TTFT distribution across their engineer population; 2) test token-budget backpressure scenarios with heavy edit churn; 3) validate model pinning + rollback latency. Links: pricing deck in Drive, FF call ids above, Jira INF-3127 opened for batching question. Short-hand follow-ups: schedule infra-level perf test, send POC checklist + eval prompts, legal to confirm residency SLA.
